chapters.name: A camera that watches your back
chapters.narration: Posture Guard is a Linux desktop posture corrector, built by Ariel Anders for the Frontier SF hackathon using Obvious AI. An Intel RealSense depth camera scores how you sit, and nudges you before the slump sticks.

cues.text: Posture Guard is a Linux desktop posture corrector, built by Ariel Anders for the Frontier SF hackathon using Obvious AI.

chapters.name: Live on the dashboard
chapters.narration: Here it is live: the pose skeleton overlaid on the camera feed, and posture metrics updating in real time. Camera-placement guidance sits beside it, and the Test button fires a nudge on demand.

chapters.name: The nudge ladder
chapters.narration: Hold a slouch and the chime fires first. Ten seconds later, a spoken prompt follows. Sit up straight for three seconds, and everything goes quiet.

chapters.name: Tuning, not code
chapters.narration: Every threshold, duration, and audio sink lives in one config file. Raise an angle threshold, stretch the voice cooldown. Tuning, not code.
